CCAT pre-trains an unbiased cross-modal classifier, which is then frozen to serve as a stable decision anchor, preventing bias toward any single modality. Modality-specific Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) modules are integrated to preserve modality-specific features during training. Additionally, a sample-level imbalance detection mechanism is employed to identify and optimize severely imbalanced samples, enhancing the representation of weaker modalities. Modality imbalance arises from disparities in information quality and optimization dynamics across different modalities, leading to gradient conflicts and suboptimal model performance. The authors observe that existing alternating training methods often fail to prevent classifier bias towards dominant modalities, thereby suppressing the contributions of weaker modalities. To mitigate this, CCAT employs a two-stage training process. First, an unbiased cross-modal classifier is pre-trained using bidirectional cross-attention and a regularization term that constrains modality contribution differences. This pre-trained classifier is then frozen during subsequent alternating training, serving as a stable decision anchor and preventing bias towards any single modality. To preserve modality-specific features while leveraging the frozen classifier, the authors integrate modality-specific Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) modules. During alternating training, only the encoder of the active modality and its corresponding LoRA parameters are updated. Additionally, a sample-level imbalance detection mechanism is introduced to identify and optimize severely imbalanced samples, further enhancing the representation of weaker modalities. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of CCAT through extensive experiments across multiple benchmark datasets, including CREMA-D, Kinetic-Sound, and MVSA. The results show significant accuracy gains over state-of-the-art methods, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in learning robust, balanced multimodal representations. This framework effectively mitigates the problem of dominant modalities suppressing weaker ones, a limitation in existing methods. This analysis provides a strong foundation for the proposed CCAT framework and demonstrates a deep understanding of the underlying issues in multimodal learning.
